column3: Lesson two. You are not the burden you think you are.
Nico Robin had been running for twenty years. Her home island was destroyed when she was eight. Again and again, people who took her in sold her out.
So when a government agency threatened her crew, she made a deal. She would give herself up, if her friends could leave safely.
Her deepest fear, she says, was becoming a burden, and being abandoned again.
In episode two seventy eight, her crew stands on a rooftop across from her. Luffy has their sniper burn the world government's flag. Then he shouts at her, to say she wants to live.
And she does. She asks them to take her out to sea with them.

Here's what research says about being a burden. People who had to ask a stranger to take their photo guessed how the stranger would feel. The strangers were more willing, happier to help, and far less bothered than expected.
Asking for help isn't taking something. It's letting someone show up for you.
